title: Cap. IX Arg. 13 Sol: grant diligence profits only those God absolutely wills to save — still no sluggishness: honor of co-working for the elect (1 Cor. iii. 9; 2 Tim. ii. 10); woe if not preach (1 Cor. ix. 16)
pass_a_gloss: But let us come yet somewhat nearer unto the matter: Grant that the diligence of ministers cannot profit except unto those whom God absolutely wills to save, and who cannot perish, yet nothing is allowed unto sluggishness nor unto sloth. First, because this very thing — to profit by one's ministry unto those whom God has exceedingly loved, and whom before the foundations of the world were laid he decreed absolutely to save — is greatly honorable and desirable. For who, in whom there is any drop of piety, if he certainly knew some infant to be predestined by God, would not labor so much the more earnestly that in promoting the same one's salvation he might be held a fellow-worker of God? 1 Cor. iii. 9. So was Paul animated, who says that all things are to be endured for the elect's sake, 2 Tim. ii. 10. Further, even that can shake torpor from ministers, that although God will by no means suffer any of the elect to perish, yet they themselves by neglecting their office incur damnable guilt, according to that of the Apostle, Woe unto me if I shall not have evangelized, 1 Cor. ix. 16.
pass_b_english: But come nearer still. Grant that ministers' diligence can profit only those God absolutely wills to save, who cannot perish — still neither sluggishness nor sloth is allowed. First: to profit by one's ministry those God has loved exceedingly, and whom before the world's foundations he decreed absolutely to save, is greatly honorable and desirable. Who, with any drop of piety, if he knew for certain some infant was predestined by God, would not labor the more earnestly to be counted God's fellow-worker in promoting that one's salvation (1 Cor. iii. 9)? So Paul was animated, who says all things are to be endured for the elect's sake (2 Tim. ii. 10). Further: even this can shake torpor from ministers — though God will not suffer any of the elect to perish, yet by neglecting their office they themselves incur damnable guilt, per the Apostle: Woe to me if I do not preach the gospel (1 Cor. ix. 16).
source_text: Verum adhuc aliquanto propius ad rem accedamus: Fac diligentiam ministrorum non posse prodesse nisi iis, quos Deus absolute vult servare, et qui perire non possunt, tamen nihil licet segnitiei neque socordiae. Primo, quia hoc ipsum prodesse suo ministerio iis, quos Deus eximie amavit, quosque ante jacta mundi fundamenta absolute servare decrevit, est valde honorificum et desiderabile. Quis enim, cui ulla inest pietatis guttula, si certo sciret aliquem infantem esse a Deo praedestinatum, non eo enixius laboraret ut in salute ejusdem promovenda Dei συνεργοὶ habeatur? 1 Cor. iii. 9. Sic Paulus animatus fuit, qui omnia propter electos sustinenda dicit, 2 Tim. ii. 10. Porro, vel illud potest ministris torporem excutere, quod licet Deus haud patietur ullum ex electis perire, tamen ipsi negligendo officium suum damnabilem reatum incurrant, juxta illud Apostoli, Vae mihi si non evangelizavero, 1 Cor. ix. 16.
